sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers four blocks deep and two blocks wide of the Lakewood hotel and business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Madison Avenue is the street at the left and Clifton Avenue the street at the centre-right, crossed from top to bottom by 7th, 6th, 5th and 4th Streets. Adjoining sheets 16 above, 4 below and 3 to the right carry the continuation. The top left block holds the Hotel Shenandoah, Carl's Ho., The Sittenreich and The Manhattan, a large frame hotel with a ball room, stage and watchman's clock. The top right block is taken up by the Clifton Av Grade School, a large brick building with an auditorium and stage, heated by steam and lit by electricity; the compass rose and the sheet's date oval are drawn beside it. The middle left block has Fairmont Lodge and its annex, Comb's Riding Academy, The Irvington, Hotel Traymore and the New Liberty Ho. East of Clifton Avenue are the Swarz Riding School, The Pine Inn and a row of dwellings. In the bottom row, west of Clifton Avenue, stand Chadwick's 5th St Garage, a long concrete block building for 100 cars, the Heyman Hotel, The Palatine and the Ferber's Strand Theatre, a brick building with balcony and stores. East of Clifton Avenue the bottom block has the Hollanders, Hotel Sachs, an autos and store building and a close row of one and two storey stores along 4th Street. Blocks are numbered 42, 43, 33, 32, 25 and 26. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are drawn in the cross streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. The sheet is closely built up, mostly with frame hotels and boarding houses.
notes: Printed names match the modern OpenStreetMap names of the same streets.
50 ft. Madison and Clifton Avs, 4th to 7th St. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 lies directly east of sheet 2 in the Lakewood hotel district and is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Lexington Avenue runs down the left centre and Monmouth Avenue near the right edge, crossed by 7th, 6th, 5th and 4th Streets. The left third of the sheet shows the blocks east of Clifton Avenue, which is lettered on sheet 2. The block above 6th Street at the left is mostly blank, holding only the compass rose and the number 43. At the top between Lexington and Monmouth Avenues stand the Hotel Embassy, a large three storey frame hotel, the Princeton Hotel, the Hotel Levitt, the Florence-in-the-Pines Annex and The Blythewood Hotel. Below 6th Street is the main building of Florence-in-the-Pines, a long wing leading down to a livery building, the Academy of St. Mary of the Lake, The Tourraine, Monmouth Paradise and The Pinewood. West of Lexington Avenue are The Pine Grove Ho., The Majestic and the Florence-in-the-Pines cottages. The bottom blocks hold a mixed set of small dwellings, The Arbutus, Conover Cottage, The Carlton and a boarding house, with shops, a tin smith, an auto repairing shop and a printing works along 4th Street at the lower left. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and 4, 6 and 8 inch water pipes are marked in the streets. Blocks are numbered 43, 32, 26, 16 above, 2, 5 and 12 around. Most of the buildings are frame hotels, boarding houses and dwellings, with few brick buildings.
notes: Printed names match the modern OpenStreetMap names of the same streets.
The block at the upper left, between 7th and 6th Streets, is blank apart from the compass rose.
50 ft. Lexington and Monmouth Avs, 4th to 7th St. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Lakewood's business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, between 4th Street at the top and 1st Street at the bottom. Madison Avenue runs down the left side and Clifton Avenue down the middle, with 3rd and 2nd Streets crossing between. Sheet 2 adjoins at the top, sheet 6 at the bottom and sheet 5 at the right. The upper left blocks hold the New Columbia and Interlaken boarding houses, the 4th St Garage, a brick garage for 80 cars, apartments over stores, and the 1st Presbyn Church. Across Clifton Avenue are The Pinehurst, the Hotel Babchin, a large brick and frame hotel with night watchman, the Municipal Bldg and the Fire Dept Junior Hose Co No. 3. The middle blocks west of Clifton Avenue hold Sharp's Lodge, All Saints Memorial Episcl Church and, at the corner of 2nd Street, a brick department store on the Clifton Avenue side with a row of brick stores along it. East of Clifton Avenue are the 1st M.E. Church, a private garage and an auto stage, a brick block of offices and halls and a row of stores along 2nd Street. The bottom row has The Monterey, The Astor Inn and a block of shops with drug stores at the left, and, east of Clifton Avenue, the Peoples Natl Bank, a garage, a furniture store and the I.O.O.F. Hall. Blocks are numbered 20, 19, 13, 14, 8 and 7. This is the closest built part of the town, with brick stores close along 2nd Street and frame hotels and houses on the outer blocks. Water pipes of 4, 6, 8 and 12 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown.
notes: Printed names match the modern OpenStreetMap names of the same streets.
50 ft. Madison and Clifton Avs, 1st to 4th St; business district. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the blocks around Lexington Avenue and Monmouth Avenue between 4th Street at the top and 1st Street at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It adjoins sheet 4 at the left, sheet 3 above, sheet 7 below and sheet 14 at the right. The upper right blocks are filled with hotels: The Marlborough Hotel, the Ardmore Hotel, Arlington Hotel, Oak Court, the Grand Hungarian Hotel and a Jewish School, with boarding houses and dwellings between. Below 3rd Street are the Y.M.C.A. with Public Library and Gymnasium, a printing works, two brick garages, Thomas Cottage and the Lakewood Library. The blocks west of Lexington Avenue hold The Hollywood, the N.J. Bell Telephone Co. building, built 1925 of fireproof construction, the Bartlett Inn and a bakery. The lower rows have Hotel Strand, the Bowling Alleys, the Laurel Ho. power house and laundry, the Biltmore Inn, and east of Lexington Avenue the Palace Theatre, a row of brick stores, a garage, the Plumbers W Ho. and the Fire Dept Hose Co. No. 1 and Hook and Ladder No. 1. At the lower right the diagonal line of the C.R.R. of N.J. is drawn with its tracks, with the Passenger Station beside them; the oblique corner of the stores and of the block at 2nd Street follows the railroad. The compass rose is at the left edge. Blocks are numbered 19, 18, 14, 15, 7 and 6, with sheet numbers 3, 4, 7 and 14 around. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked in the streets.
notes: Printed names match the modern OpenStreetMap names of the same streets.
The Central Railroad of New Jersey (printed C.R.R. of N.J.) and the Passenger Station are drawn at the lower right.
50 ft. Lexington and Monmouth Avs, 1st to 4th St; C.R.R. of N.J. at right. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the southern edge of Lakewood's business district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. 1st Street runs along the top; Madison Avenue is the street at the left edge, Clifton Avenue runs down the upper middle and continues south as Meadow Av, and Main crosses the sheet roughly halfway down. Sheet 4 adjoins above, sheet 7 at the right and sheet 25 below. The upper left block, between 1st Street and Main, holds a close row of brick and frame stores along Clifton Avenue, with the Hotel Virginia, a bank building with a vault and offices, a drug store and a tea house among them. Across Clifton Avenue the 1st Baptist Church stands at the top, and the Laurel House hotel, with its West Wing and Musik Room, is cut off at the right edge with a reference to the report on sheet 7. South of Main are St. Mary of the Lake R.C. Church, St. Mary's Hall, a bakery, an auto storage and a row of shops at the Meadow Av corner, with a row of dwellings and shops east of Meadow Av facing Main. Below Main the sheet is mostly open, with blocks lettered A and B, a few scattered buildings along Meadow Av, an open water course crossing near the foot of the sheet, and the words Low Marsh Land spread across the lower right. A large blue building stands at the lower left corner. The compass rose is at the lower right. Blocks are numbered 3, 4, 43 and 25 below and the water pipes of 6, 8 and 12 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are drawn in the streets.
notes: Main is printed without a suffix; it is Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
Meadow Av, the road running south from Main, is South Clifton Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from few control points: Madison Avenue is cut by the sheet edge and the Main Street and Clifton Avenue junction lies several metres from the drawn pipe crossing.
50 ft. Madison and Clifton Avs south of 1st St, Main, Meadow Av (South Clifton Avenue), creek and low land; exact fit through 3 points (one carried from sheet 4). Low confidence.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the southeastern edge of Lakewood's centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, where the business streets meet the Central Railroad of New Jersey. 1st Street runs along the top, Lexington Avenue down the left centre, and Main, continuing east as Ocean Av, crosses the sheet below the middle. Sheet 6 adjoins at the left, sheet 5 above, sheet 14 at the right and sheet 25 below. The left upper block is filled by the Laurel House, a large frame hotel with dining room, east and west wings, a reading room, billiard room and a platform, with its own hose, watchmen and fire protection described in a note. East of Lexington Avenue are Gray Gables, a laundry, St. John's church, an auto repairing shop, a large livery and private autos building, The Lexington Garage and The Lexington hotel. South of Main stand the Towers Hotel, an auto show room, Lakewood Garage, a brick garage for 80 cars, and Hotel Affronti. The double and triple tracks of the C.R.R. of N.J. run diagonally across the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, with a branch swinging south along a wood coal trestle. Along the tracks are the Freight Ho., an oil storage, an office building and groceries, the C. R. Le Compte Coal Co. yard, Chas. Lewis Jr. Lumber and Mill Work with long lumber sheds, a planing mill and carpenter shop, and the Ocean Av. Ho. The lower left of the sheet is open ground with a cistern and the words Low Marsh Land. Blocks are numbered 4, 5, 110 and 306, and the compass rose is at the lower left. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are drawn along the streets.
notes: Main is printed without a suffix; it is Main Street in OpenStreetMap.
Ocean Av is the continuation of Main east of the railroad; OpenStreetMap carries it as Ocean Avenue.
The railroad is printed C.R.R. of N.J. and is the Southern Secondary in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft. Lexington Av, 1st St, Main, Ocean Av and the railroad; 4 points (one carried from sheet 5, one rail crossing). Low to medium confidence.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers six blocks of the hotel and boarding-house quarter in the centre of Lakewood, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Two columns of blocks lie either side of Forest Avenue, with Madison Avenue running down the right edge of the sheet, and the rows are separated by 9th, 8th, 7th and 6th Streets from top to bottom. The left column is largely open: lots with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings at the top, a large house and carriage barn behind a Private Way at the left edge in the middle, and a brick and frame dwelling and a stand pipe fed by an 8 inch water main in the lower block. The right column is built up with hotels and lodging houses. The New Grand Hotel and the New Brighton Hotel stand in the block below 9th Street, with a large dwelling to their west and a compass rose drawn in the open ground between. In the middle block are The Balfour, The Marquette (heated by steam and lit by electricity) and several smaller dwellings, with brick-trimmed first floors on the Madison Avenue frontage. The bottom block holds the New Telavvy Hotel, The New Edgewood, Berger Villa, Benevy Lodge, Schoharie Mansion and Helferd Lodge, with frame dwellings and many small outbuildings between. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet are lettered, and 6 and 8 inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown along the streets. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins as 15 above, 16 to the right and 10 below.
notes: Forest Avenue and Madison Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Names of the buildings New Telavvy Hotel, Benevy Lodge and Helferd Lodge are read from small lettering and may be misread (low confidence).
The sheet is drawn square to the page while its streets run about 8.5 degrees from north; the fit rotation is 8.5 degrees.
50 ft. Forest and Madison Avs, 6th to 9th St; hotel quarter. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and shows the Laurel-in-the-Pines hotel grounds on the north shore of Lake Carasaljo, in the north-west of Lakewood. The upper edge is 5th Street, drawn as a long straight street with a six-inch water pipe, and the right edge is the Private Way, a narrow lane running down the sheet from 5th Street to 2nd Street, with 4th Street shown only as a dashed water-pipe line entering it from the east. Lake Drive crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right between the hotel and the lake. Most of the sheet is occupied by the Laurel-in-the-Pines hotel, a large complex of connected buildings with ball room, dining room, palm room, office, kitchen, laundry and ice house, enclosed by a dotted line marking the hotel property and ringed by hydrants and water pipes, with a note on the watchmen, clocks, heat, hose and ladders. Along 5th Street stand the hotel garage, a hotel hospital, a plumber's shop and several frame dwellings, with sheds behind them. At the upper left the Arden School stands beside a dotted lot line. The lower left is open water: Lake Carasaljo, with its shore line and an inlet near the bottom. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the lower left. Only three junctions along the Private Way are available, so the placement rests on two points and is low confidence.
notes: Placed from two points on the Private Way (5th Street, and 4th Street, which the sheet draws only as a dashed water-pipe line); the 2nd Street junction did not agree with the modern node (about 7 percent in distance) and was not used.
Lake Drive is today North Lake Drive; the Private Way is still called Private Way in OpenStreetMap.
The Laurel-in-the-Pines hotel is gone; the district is now residential.
50 ft. Laurel-in-the-Pines hotel grounds on Lake Carasaljo, Private Way, Lake Drive; two-point helmert. Low confidence.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 continues the hotel and boarding-house quarter of central Lakewood south of sheet 8, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Two columns of blocks lie either side of Forest Avenue, with Madison Avenue along the right edge, and the cross streets 6th, 5th, 4th and 3rd run down the page. The left column is mostly open ground: small frame dwellings from plans (lettered A, B and C) at the top, the New Atlantic Hotel and the New Hotel Adler (both heated by steam and lit by electricity) in the top block next to Forest Avenue, a large open block with the compass rose in the middle, flanked by a Private Way at the left edge with a large barn and a few dwellings, and scattered dwellings and one brick building in the lower blocks. The right column is closely built with hotels and boarding houses. The Hotel Belmont, Paradise and the Sun Ray Cottage are in the top block below 6th Street; Hotel Gotham, the New Ellenson Ho. and Zwebens White Ho. occupy the middle row of blocks, the last at Madison Avenue; and the lowest row holds Woltos Villa, The Fairview Lodge, The Lakeview, the F.J. Schwarz Riding School, The Washington and the Hotel Vendome. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes run along the streets, and the street widths of 60 and 80 feet are lettered. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins as 8 above, 11 below, 15 and 9 to the left and 2 and 4 to the right.
notes: Forest Avenue and Madison Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
The numbers 8 above and 11 below are neighbouring sheets; 15, 9, 2 and 4 in the left and right margins are read from the margins and may be other sheets or volumes.
50 ft. Forest and Madison Avs, 3rd to 6th St. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the south-western edge of central Lakewood at 50 feet to an inch, where the street grid meets the shore of Lake Carasaljo. Forest Avenue and Madison Avenue run down the page, crossed by 3rd, 2nd and 1st Streets; a Private Way and a curving Lake Drive follow the left and lower edges, and the lake itself is drawn as a blue band across the lower left corner. The blocks east of Forest Avenue are the built-up part: Sunset Lodge, The Schulman Ho. and several frame and brick dwellings between 3rd and 2nd Streets; Ritter's Hotel, a club house, a filling station near Madison Avenue and two large buildings coloured blue (fire-resistive or non-dwelling construction) between 2nd and 1st Streets; and, below 1st Street, Adler Cottage, The Madison Hotel, Hotel Armen and further dwellings and outbuildings, with the lower blocks cut off along the curve of Lake Drive. West of Forest Avenue the land is mostly open: a few dwellings along the Private Way at the top left, large unsubdivided tracts with one or two houses, and wide lake-front parcels bounded by the two long diagonal lines of Lake Drive. A compass rose and the lettering Lake Carasaljo occupy the lower left. Street widths of 60 and 80 feet are lettered, with 6 and 8 inch water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins as 10 above, 6 and 4 to the right and 9 to the left.
notes: Lake Drive is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name and is left out of the fit; the drawn Lake Drive follows the shore of Lake Carasaljo.
Forest Avenue and Madison Avenue keep their names in OpenStreetMap.
Hotel Armen and other building names are read from the full-resolution scan; the lettering on Zwebens, Ritter's and Schulman buildings was read on the overview-scale crop only (medium confidence).
50 ft. Forest and Madison Avs, 1st to 3rd St, Lake Carasaljo and Lake Drive at lower left. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers a block-by-block strip of Lakewood east of the hotel quarter, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Monmouth Avenue runs down the left edge and Princeton Avenue down the middle, crossed by 7th, 6th, 5th and 4th Streets from top to bottom. At the top right is the Lakewood High School, a large brick building with gymnasium and auditorium, heated by steam and lit by electricity, standing in its own block with a compass rose beside it. The blocks between Monmouth and Princeton Avenues are residential, with frame dwellings (The Pine Crest, Sunnyside, Belvoir Cottage, The Rose Villa, Carmel Ho.) and the 6th Baptist Church between 7th and 6th Streets; below 5th Street the lots turn commercial, with a planing mill, lumber yard, John Grant's Sons Inc. with a garage and woodworking and painting shops, tenements, a bakery, the Lincoln Hotel and Auto Sales Service on 4th Street. East of Princeton Avenue the blocks hold dwellings and small industry: a machine shop, a lumber shed, a warehouse and the So. Jersey Sash Door & Trim Co. manufacturing plant, the Levinson Clothing Co. factory (frame, not in operation), the Glendale Farms Dairy and a railroad heating plant. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs diagonally from the upper right to the lower left with several tracks, and the lower right corner is occupied by Front, Ridge Av. and E. 4th St. drawn at an angle, with the scale bar. Water pipes of 6 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown; the street widths of 60, 80 and 50 feet are lettered. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins as 17 above, 14 below, 13 to the right and 3 to the left.
notes: Front (no suffix printed) does not appear under that name in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The drawn Ridge Av. and E. 4th St. meet Princeton Avenue at one OpenStreetMap node (4th Street / East 4th Street / Princeton Avenue / Ridge Avenue).
The railroad shown is the Central Railroad of New Jersey (Southern Secondary in OpenStreetMap).
50 ft. Monmouth and Princeton Avs, 4th to 7th St, railroad at right. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the northeast edge of Lakewood's town centre at 50 feet to an inch, where the street grid breaks into diagonal streets on either side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey. East 4th Street runs along the bottom of the sheet with East 5th Street above it, joined by Ridgefourth running north to south and by the diagonal Ridge Av., which crosses the sheet from lower left to upper right and meets Maple Av. at the top right corner. Front runs along the east side of the railroad tracks in the upper left and ends in a wedge at the Auto Repairing garage, a blue-coloured concrete building with an earth floor, heated by stoves and lit by electricity. Hackett crosses the upper right, with long narrow lots laid out between Front, Ridge Av. and Hackett and mostly occupied by single frame dwellings and outbuildings; a few boarding houses, a private hospital and a house named Ridgewood stand along Ridge Av. Along East 4th Street the lots are commercial and densely built with stores and a large department store, a mattress factory, a synagogue in the lower left, a feed store and, further east, a vacant brick building and a concrete storage building. Jersey Av. is lettered not opened along the right edge, and Linwood Av. is lettered at the bottom left. Street widths of 25, 35, 36, 40, 45 and 50 feet are lettered, with 4 and 6 inch water pipes. A compass rose stands at the upper left, and the printed 6th St. stub appears in the left margin beside the railroad. Neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins as 17 above, 12 to the left, 14 and 20 below and 19 above right.
notes: Ridgefourth is Ridge 4th Street in OpenStreetMap.
Hackett is Hacket Street in OpenStreetMap.
Front (no suffix printed) does not appear under that name in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Jersey Av. is lettered not opened (drawn but not opened in 1928).
Ridgewood in quotation marks beside a boarding house is read as a house name, not a street.
The scale bar shows 50 feet to an inch, confirming the scale judged for this sheet.
50 ft. East 4th and 5th St, Ridge Av, Ridgefourth (Ridge 4th Street), Front, Hackett (Hacket Street), Maple Av, Jersey Av; drawn north up (rotation near 0, neighbours +8). One part.

sheet-14-1.description: The main part of sheet 14, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the area south of the Lakewood business district where the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the town. A broad bundle of tracks runs diagonally from the lower left to the top centre. West of the tracks, along Monmouth Avenue between 4th Street and 2nd Street, is the end of the downtown commercial strip: shops, a plumbing store, the Post Office, the Y.W.C.A., an auto show room with a milk station and apartments along 4th Street, and a large concrete block garage for eighty cars near 2nd Street, with a filling station beside it. East of the tracks, at the top right, E. 4th Street carries a feed mill and a row of dwellings, with the Lakewood Coal Co. trestle and spur running beside Front St., and Linwood Avenue runs along the right edge. Below the tracks at the lower left the part shows only the edge of the railroad land and buildings drawn on neighbouring sheets. A heavy line separates this part from the lumber yard and Ocean Avenue blocks at the lower right, which are drawn apart from it on the page.
notes: The modern streets Steckler Street, Park Avenue South, Kedma Drive and Yomah Court cross drawn blocks.
Placed from two parcel block corners on Monmouth Avenue (hand-picked), 665 ft apart: low confidence away from Monmouth Avenue.
Front St. is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.

50 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Monmouth Av between 4th and 2nd St, the C.R.R. of N.J., E. 4th St, Front St, Linwood Av; helmert from two hand-picked parcel block corners. Part 2 (lower right inside heavy line, drawn apart on the page): Ocean Av, A. A. Brant Lumber Co., Not Named street (Congress Street) and Bruce St; helmert from two detected junctions.

sheet-14-2.description: This part of sheet 14, at the lower right inside a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows the blocks along Ocean Avenue east of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, set apart on the page from the rest of the sheet. Ocean Avenue crosses the lower part from west to east with 6 and 8 inch water pipes. A street lettered Not Named runs north from Ocean Avenue along the right side, and Bruce St. runs east from it near the top right. The large block north of Ocean Avenue holds the A. A. Brant Lumber Co. yard, with its lumber piles, a long lumber shed and a siding, a furniture store with storage, a concrete block storage and auto building and the Duco Auto Paint Shop, and a filling station near Ocean Avenue. South of Ocean Avenue stand Claytons Garage, a concrete block building for fifty cars with a machine shop, an auto repair shop, stores and a few dwellings. A compass rose sits on the heavy line at the top. The bottom edge is marked no exposure.
notes: The street lettered Not Named is Congress Street in OpenStreetMap.

This part was first configured with the main part as one; its streets then lay 18 to 30 m from the modern ones. Placed on its own from Congress Street at Ocean Avenue and at Bruce Street (helmert, 8.18 px/ft): low to medium confidence.

50 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): Monmouth Av between 4th and 2nd St, the C.R.R. of N.J., E. 4th St, Front St, Linwood Av; helmert from two hand-picked parcel block corners. Part 2 (lower right inside heavy line, drawn apart on the page): Ocean Av, A. A. Brant Lumber Co., Not Named street (Congress Street) and Bruce St; helmert from two detected junctions.

sheet-15-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 15 and covers the west side of Lakewood between Lake Carasaljo and Private Way, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Lakewood Avenue runs down the left side of the built blocks, and 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th Streets cross the sheet to the east. The blocks between 9th and 7th Streets are almost entirely vacant, numbered 153 and 154 and divided only by lot lines, with a stable and a few dwellings at the east end of block 154. Between 7th and 6th Streets block 155 holds a few large dwellings and outbuildings, and the block above 5th Street holds a row of small frame dwellings and outbuildings on narrow lots facing Private Way. At the upper left stands the large Casino building, lettered Formerly The Casino, with racquet courts, a tennis court auditorium, lounge, bowling alley and apartments, served by a four inch water pipe. West of Lakewood Avenue are the Sisters of Mercy grounds, with a chapel, laboratory, class rooms and dwellings enclosed by a dashed line and marked no watchman, and a long frame building beyond. Lake Drive, sixty feet wide, curves across the lower left past Lake Carasaljo, whose shore is tinted blue. The left margin is lettered No Exposure. A box at the top right, set off by a heavy line, is a separate part showing Forest and Madison Avenues and is described separately; a compass and north arrow stand just left of it. Block numbers 104, 151, 152, 153, 154, 155, 156 and 254 appear, and neighbouring sheet numbers 8, 9 and 10 are printed in the margins.
notes: Lake Drive is North Lake Drive in OpenStreetMap; the modern road along the shore is displaced from the drawn one.
Private Way is drawn at the right edge, partly cut by the sheet; its modern line did not agree with the drawn street, so it was not used for control.
All control points of this part lie along Lakewood Avenue, so rotation and scale rest on points along one line.
The box at the top right is a different place on the ground: Forest and Madison Avenues are about 520 m east of Lakewood Avenue.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Lakewood Av, 5th to 9th St, Lake Drive (helmert along Lakewood Av, low confidence); part 2 (box at top right) Forest and Madison Avs at 9th and 10th St, about 520 m east of part 1 on the ground.

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 is the box at the top right of sheet 15, separated from the main map by a heavy line, and covers the corner of Forest Avenue and Madison Avenue between 9th and 10th Streets in the hotel quarter of Lakewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Forest Avenue runs down the left side and Madison Avenue down the right; 10th Street crosses the middle and 9th Street runs along the heavy line at the bottom, which is the sheet's own border. The block between Forest and Madison Avenues, numbered 158, holds two large hotels with their grounds: the yellow Hotel Brunswick, a frame building, and the Hotel Grossman, a brick building with a laundry, both equipped with watchman, clock, heat, steam and electric lights. The block above 10th Street holds the Hotel Stanley at the right, a large pink building with several wings. Block numbers 157, 158 and 271 appear, with neighbouring sheet numbers 8 and 16 at the margins. The Lakewood, N.J., July 1928 stamp is at the top. The streets are sixty feet wide and carry four inch and six inch water pipes with hydrants and fire alarm boxes.
notes: This box is drawn at the same scale as the main map but shows a different part of town about 520 m to the east.
9th Street, at the bottom of the box, is a boundary street drawn with only one edge before the heavy sheet border.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Lakewood Av, 5th to 9th St, Lake Drive (helmert along Lakewood Av, low confidence); part 2 (box at top right) Forest and Madison Avs at 9th and 10th St, about 520 m east of part 1 on the ground.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the residential grid north of the Lakewood business district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It runs from 7th Street at the bottom to Courtney Road and 12th Street at the top, and from Madison Avenue on the west to Monmouth Avenue on the east, with Clifton Avenue and Lexington Avenue between them; the cross streets are 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th Streets and Cary, with 13th Street lettered at the top left and at the right edge. Most blocks are laid out in narrow house lots and are still largely vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and their outbuildings. The southern blocks hold the hotel quarter: the very large building lettered formerly The Lakewood, a frame and brick hotel shown vacant and dilapidated in the block between Clifton and Lexington Avenues above 7th Street, and around it the New Winthrop Hotel, the Clarendon Hotel, the Safran, Schildkraut's Hotel, the Bohemian Frumkin Villa, Hotel Tavern, the New Forest and Mayflower hotels, the Rosedale Hotel, the New Hotel Hoffman, the New Irvington hotel, the New Beverly Hotel, New Kriegel's Hotel, the Hotel Monmouth and the Pine Inn. Mrs. C. Fischel's Boarding School stands on Madison Avenue between 11th Street and Cary, and two concrete block public garages face Madison Avenue near 10th Street. Water pipes of 2 to 8 inches are drawn along most streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. 9th Street between Clifton and Lexington Avenues and 8th Street between Lexington and Monmouth Avenues are marked not opened. Squankum Road appears at the lower right corner. A north arrow and compass rose sit in the block between Madison Avenue and Clifton Avenue below 12th Street.
notes: Cary (no suffix printed) is Carey Street in OpenStreetMap.
The hotel formerly The Lakewood is shown vacant and dilapidated.
9th Street between Clifton and Lexington Avenues and 8th Street between Lexington and Monmouth Avenues are marked not opened (drawn but not opened in 1928).
100 ft. Pilot. Madison, Clifton, Lexington and Monmouth Avenues between 7th Street and Courtney Road; Cary (modern Carey Street); hotel quarter with the vacant former The Lakewood hotel.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the north-central part of Lakewood east of the business district, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The western half is a regular grid between Monmouth Avenue on the left and Princeton Avenue, cut by 13th, 11th, 10th, 9th, 8th and 7th Streets from top to bottom, with Cary Street entering at the top left. Many of the northern blocks are large and nearly empty, the 11th Street blocks hold scattered frame dwellings on narrow lots, and 13th Street and the eastern end of 9th Street are marked not opened. Hotels dominate the southern blocks: Hotel Nisselson at 9th Street and Monmouth Avenue, Monmouth-in-the-Pines, Hotel Lorrain and Irene Court at 7th Street, Hotel Sonnet, the Silver Cottage and Young Pine Villa between 8th and 7th Streets, and Feldman's Hotel and Traubs Villa on Princeton Avenue. A Monmouth Garage for forty cars stands where Squankum Road cuts diagonally across the grid. Squankum Road and the short diagonal Lawrence Avenue run north-east across the sheet, with a cement block manufactory beside 10th Street and Lawrence Avenue. At the lower right the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs south-west as a bundle of tracks with a grand stand beside it and Burns Bros Coal Yard at 7th Street; Park Avenue and Front Street run past it, with Hackett Street branching off Front Street at the bottom. The upper right is nearly blank paper with a few scattered dwellings near the sheet edge. Block numbers and neighbouring sheet numbers 12, 13, 16, 18 and 19 are printed in the margins.
notes: Cary Street is Carey Street in OpenStreetMap.
Squankum Road and Lawrence Avenue are drawn 4 to 5 m off their modern lines and were left out of the control.
13th Street and the eastern end of 9th Street are marked not opened.
Front Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract under that name.
100 ft. Monmouth and Princeton Avs, 6th to 13th St, Squankum Rd and Lawrence Av (both left out, 4 to 5 m off), Park Av, railroad. One part; no control east of Princeton Av.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the north-eastern edge of the built-up town of Lakewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The Central Railroad of New Jersey runs diagonally from the lower left to the top centre as a pair of tracks with a strip of long narrow lots along its east side, and Park Avenue runs parallel to it on the east. East of Park Avenue lies a large subdivision of narrow building lots laid out between Park Avenue and East End Avenue and cut by East Harvard Street, Leonard Street, Rosebank Street, East 9th Street and East 8th Street; most of the lots are still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings near East Harvard Street and Leonard Street, and a garage for seventy-five cars on East Harvard Street. East End Avenue forms the eastern boundary of the built blocks, and a further group of long lots lies beyond it. At the lower left, between the railroad and Park Avenue, are industrial plants: John F. Brown and Son coal and wood, a Standard Oil Company of New Jersey depot, the Gulf Refining Company station and a dry cleaning works, with Ziegler Bros. carpet cleaning beside Park Avenue. The top of the sheet is crossed by the dash-dot line of the Monmouth County and Ocean County boundary, along County Line Road, with Lakewood Township lettered on the Ocean County side. North of Harvard Street are larger plots with scattered dwellings, Apple Street, Park Place and Squankum Road on the western edge, and the pine woods on the upper right. The lower left corner carries a few buildings of the neighbouring sheets 17 and 19, and the lower right is blank paper.
notes: Harvard, Apple, Leonard and Rosebank are printed without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Harvard Street, Apple Street, Leonard Street and Rosebank Street.
Park Avenue is also lettered with the alternative name Railroad Avenue in brackets north of Rosebank; OpenStreetMap has a separate Railroad Avenue and Railroad Street here.
County Line Road follows the Monmouth and Ocean County line; the modern road is East County Line.
A township name lettered on the Monmouth County side of the boundary line is struck through and could not be read with confidence.
The street at the lower left lettered Ninth Street lies beyond the railroad on sheet 17's side.
100 ft. Park Av to East End Av: East 8th and 9th St, Harvard, Rosebank, Leonard, Nowlan Pl, Monmouth County line. One part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the east side of the old town of Lakewood, east of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, at 100 feet to an inch, and is drawn turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page. Ridge Avenue is the main street; it climbs from the bottom edge, bends around a curve at the top left and runs north-west toward Hackett Street, with Maple Avenue branching east along the top and Front Street and Park Avenue crossing the top edge. In the upper right, East 7th Street and Nowlan Place run south-east past narrow house lots and two lanes marked not named, with the Grand Pine Hotel beside Westwood Avenue. On the left, East 4th Street runs south through a built-up residential district, crossed by Jersey Avenue, South, Dewey Avenue, Sampson Avenue and Manetta Avenue, with Clover Street and School Street at the bottom and Public School No. 5 inside the block between East 4th Street and North Holly, which is also lettered Sherwood Avenue. An Ideal Steam Laundry, a drug store and a Gospel Mission stand along East 4th Street and North Holly. The middle of the sheet is open ground, much of it the athletic field. Manetta Avenue appears twice, once among the left-hand blocks and again as a diagonal street across the lower middle toward Ridge Avenue, which continues south along the right side past a row of dwellings and a chicken house to the bottom. Neighbouring sheets 13, 17, 18, 20 and 21 are named in the margins.
notes: Front and Hackett are printed without a suffix; Hackett is Hacket Street in OpenStreetMap, and Front Street is not in the extract under that name.
South is printed without a suffix; the modern name is South Street.
North Holly is lettered with Sherwood Avenue in brackets.
Two lanes in the upper right are lettered not named.
Park Avenue crosses the top of the sheet and meets Front Street at the neighbouring sheet 17.

100 ft. Turned about 54 degrees from the grid sheets. Ridge Av, Manetta Av, Nowlan Pl, South, School St, East 4th to 7th St, Maple, Hackett, Front, N. Holly (Sherwood Av). One part; several streets 5 to 9 m off left out.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the south-eastern part of Lakewood's old town, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. East 4th Street crosses the top of the sheet as a long row of closely built frame dwellings and shops, from Linwood Avenue and a lane lettered Driveway at the left to a bend at the upper right, where Dewey Avenue and Sampson Avenue run south-west from it past a wagon works, a bakery and a fire department with its rescue company. Bergen Avenue forms the lower edge of that wedge of blocks. The central and lower part of the sheet is a grid of Congress, Pearl and Clover streets crossed by Bruce, Ocean Avenue and Laurel Avenue. Ocean Avenue and Laurel Avenue carry rows of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a garage and a machine shop on the western block near Congress, and a large garage with a bus garage on Congress and Ocean Avenue. At the lower right corner stand the buildings and gas holders of the Lakewood Gas Works beside Clover. A large empty tract lies north of Ocean Avenue between Pearl and Clover, and the blocks along Congress and Bruce are mostly vacant, with a few scattered houses. Streets at the upper left, Linwood Avenue and the lane lettered Driveway, belong to the district continued on sheet 14; a block at the left is lettered No Name. Neighbouring sheets 13, 14, 19 and 21 are named in the margins, and block numbers 108, 185, 186, 190, 191, 196 and 197 appear on the sheet.
notes: Bruce, Congress, Pearl and Clover are printed without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Bruce Street, Congress Street, Pearl Street and Clover Street.
A street at the left edge is lettered No Name.
Laurel Avenue between Congress and Pearl is lettered not opened.
The drawn east-west spacing of the streets in the southern half is about 4 percent shorter than the modern streets, so the fitted scale is about 3.83 pixels per foot against 4.0 on the scale bar.
Ridgefouth St. is printed so (spelled Ridgefourth on sheet 13 and in the index); it is Ridge 4th Street in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. East 4th St east of Linwood Av, Ridgefouth St (printed so), Bruce, Congress, Pearl, Clover, Dewey, Sampson, Manetta, Bergen, Ocean and Laurel Avs. Drawn about 6 percent short east-west. One part.

sheet-21-1.description: The main part of sheet 21 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the district east of Lakewood's business centre, between Clover Street on the west and Oakland Street on the east, with Ocean Avenue crossing the lower part of the sheet from side to side. In the upper part Ridge Avenue runs across the top between blocks of small frame dwellings, with Manetta Avenue running up to the upper left from a point near the left edge, and North Holly, lettered as Sherwood Av., running diagonally from the left edge down to Holly. Below these, School Street joins East 4th Street at the lower left, and Bergen Avenue crosses Holly between the blocks above Ocean Avenue. South of Bergen Avenue the blocks between Clover and Holly Streets hold a suit factory with steam heat and electric light, a large building in blue, and rows of frame dwellings; a machine shop and garage lettered Wallace is shown on Holly Street. Along Ocean Avenue stand Ocean Av Inn at the corner of Clover Street and rows of dwellings, with Laurel Avenue lettered at the foot of the sheet. Linden runs north from Ocean Avenue past Sterling Av., which is drawn as a short street, and the large area in the middle of the sheet is block 184, 193 and 194, mostly vacant. A boxed inset at the right, with a heavy outline, is a separate part. A compass rose stands to its lower right and a scale bar is at the foot.
notes: Ocean Avenue, Clover, Holly, Bergen and Linden are today Ocean Avenue, Clover Street, Holly Street, Bergen Avenue and Linden Avenue; Oakland is South Oakland Street south of Ocean Avenue.
Linden Avenue junctions lie about 3 m from the fit to the other streets.
Ridge Avenue, Manetta Avenue and the diagonal North Holly (Sherwood Av.) were not used for control: their modern lines do not match the drawn ones closely enough.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Ridge Av, Manetta Av, N. Holly, School St, Bergen Av, Clover, Holly, Linden, Sterling Av, Ocean Av, Oakland, Laurel Av; part 2 (box at top right) Laurel Av between Clover and Holly, two-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21 is the heavy-lined box at the upper right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows the block between Clover and Holly Streets south of Laurel Avenue, the ground below the foot of the main part, which stops at Laurel Avenue. Laurel Avenue runs along the top of the box with its water pipe, Clover is lettered along the left side of the box and Holly along the right, and the block between them, numbered 201, is cut into long narrow lots running south to the lower edge of the box, which is marked No Exposure. A few frame dwellings face Laurel Avenue, numbered 402 to 432, together with a shed, and a carpet cleaning works, the Lakewood Carpet Cleaning Works, stands near Clover Street with its steam heat and electric light. A building at the right edge beyond Holly Street is shown in yellow and blue. The number 20 at the left marks the neighbouring sheet. A compass rose stands below the right half of the box, outside it. The part is placed from two junctions, Clover Street and Holly Street at Laurel Avenue, one measured and one hand-picked, so it is low confidence.
notes: Holly Street at Laurel Avenue was hand-picked because Holly Street has no arm south of Laurel Avenue in the modern data.
Placed as a two-point helmert; its fitted scale is 1.2 percent below the main part.

100 ft. Two parts: part 1 (main) Ridge Av, Manetta Av, N. Holly, School St, Bergen Av, Clover, Holly, Linden, Sterling Av, Ocean Av, Oakland, Laurel Av; part 2 (box at top right) Laurel Av between Clover and Holly, two-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-22-1.description: The main part of sheet 22, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the south edge of John D. Rockefeller's estate east of the Lakewood village grid, along Ocean Avenue. Ocean Avenue crosses the lower half of the part, running straight east from Oakland at the left edge and then bending southeast towards the right edge, with a 6 inch water pipe laid in it. Cherry runs north from Ocean Avenue near the left edge, and Oakland is drawn south of Ocean Avenue along the left margin with its narrow house lots. The block between Oakland and Cherry north of Ocean Avenue holds a few frame dwellings, automobile garages and hen houses, and east of Cherry a large tract lettered John D. Rockefeller's Estate holds scattered dwellings, garages, sheds and stables. South of Ocean Avenue the land is mostly undivided, with a row of small dwellings near Oakland and a few more along the bend of Ocean Avenue at the lower right. The rest of the part is open ground. A compass rose stands in the estate tract, and the scale bar is printed at the bottom. Heavy lines separate this part from the estate interior and the Ridge Avenue blocks above it and from an inset at the right showing a cement block works elsewhere on Ocean Avenue.
notes: Cherry (no suffix printed) is Cherry Street in OpenStreetMap; Oakland south of Ocean Avenue is South Oakland Street.
The Rockefeller estate is now Ocean County Park.
Placed from one detected junction (Ocean Avenue and Cherry) with the atlas scale; the hand-picked Ocean Avenue and Oakland junction lies about 5 m from the fit.

100 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (main, bottom): Ocean Avenue with Cherry and Oakland and the south edge of John D. Rockefeller's Estate (now Ocean County Park); anchored on Ocean/Cherry. Part 2 (top left): interior of the Rockefeller estate, no streets. Part 3 (top right): Ridge Av (modern East 7th Street), Brook Rd (modern Ridge Avenue east of the junction) and Ridge Av running south (modern curved Ridge Avenue), Beechwood Av (gone); anchored on one junction. Part 4 (inset, right): Garfield Herbert cement block works on Ocean Av, 2.5 miles from Madison and Main Avenues.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top left: interior of John D. Rockefeller's Estate (buildings only) (no street or junction drawn; needs hand-picked control on estate buildings surviving in Ocean County Park, if any).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Garfield Herbert cement block manufacturing on Ocean Avenue, 2.5 miles from Madison and Main Avenues (one street, no junction; needs identification of the site along Ocean Avenue (NJ 88) and parcel corners).

sheet-22-3.description: This part of sheet 22, at the upper right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows a small group of residential blocks east of the Lakewood village. A road along the top is lettered Ridge Av. to the west of a junction and Brook Rd. to the east of it; from that junction Ridge Av. runs south down the part, and Beechwood Av. runs east from it, marked not graded at its west end. The block west of Ridge Avenue, numbered 217, and the blocks east of it, 218 and 219, are laid out in lots with a scattering of frame dwellings, automobile garages and sheds, most of them along Ridge Avenue. North of the top road, block 216 has a few more dwellings, and Mt. Sinai Cemetery is noted beyond it at the top margin. Large parts of the blocks are empty, and the edges are marked no exposure. A north arrow is drawn at the upper left of the part. Heavy lines separate it from the Rockefeller estate to the left and from the Ocean Avenue part below.
notes: The top road lettered Ridge Av. west of the junction is East 7th Street in OpenStreetMap; Brook Rd. east of the junction is now part of Ridge Avenue; Ridge Av. running south is the curved Ridge Avenue of today.
Beechwood Av. is not in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one junction (Ridge Avenue, Brook Road and East 7th Street) with the atlas scale and rotation from its measured lines: low confidence.

100 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (main, bottom): Ocean Avenue with Cherry and Oakland and the south edge of John D. Rockefeller's Estate (now Ocean County Park); anchored on Ocean/Cherry. Part 2 (top left): interior of the Rockefeller estate, no streets. Part 3 (top right): Ridge Av (modern East 7th Street), Brook Rd (modern Ridge Avenue east of the junction) and Ridge Av running south (modern curved Ridge Avenue), Beechwood Av (gone); anchored on one junction. Part 4 (inset, right): Garfield Herbert cement block works on Ocean Av, 2.5 miles from Madison and Main Avenues.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Garfield Herbert cement block manufacturing on Ocean Avenue, 2.5 miles from Madison and Main Avenues (one street, no junction; needs identification of the site along Ocean Avenue (NJ 88) and parcel corners).

sheet-23-1.description: The main part of sheet 23, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows a residential subdivision along Central Avenue west of Lake Carasaljo, on the western side of Lakewood. Central Avenue crosses the lower middle of the part from Columbus Avenue at the left edge to the right edge, where it continues on sheet 24. Two short streets lettered not named cross Central Avenue east of Columbus Avenue, one 40 feet and one 25 feet wide. Montray Circle is the main feature: a broad curving street that leaves Central Avenue, sweeps north and west to end in a turning loop, and to the south swings round in a wide arc back to Central Avenue, with a small oval loop of road straddling Central Avenue inside it. The blocks, numbered 310 to 319 and 287, are cut into lots, many of them wedge shaped around the circle, and most are vacant; frame dwellings with automobile garages and hen houses are scattered along Central Avenue and the circle. Some lot lines in the northern blocks are marked from plans. A block lettered G lies at the right between Central Avenue and a diagonal line. A compass rose stands at the upper left, and the scale bar is at the lower left. A heavy line separates this part from the golf links drawing above and from the Central Avenue blocks between Carlton and Columbus Avenues at the top right.
notes: Montray Circle is Monterey Circle and Circle Place in OpenStreetMap; the small oval is North Monterey Court and Monterey Court South.
The two streets lettered not named are Saint Nicholas Avenue and Hollywood Avenue today.
Control lies along Central Avenue only, so the part is fitted as a helmert (position, scale and rotation).

Three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (main, bottom, 100 ft): Central Av, Columbus Av and Montray Circle (modern Monterey Circle and Circle Place). Part 2 (top, 200 ft to an inch): Country Club's Golf Links, Newman School, Hope Chapel Rd (North Hope Chapel Road), 14th St, Lake Drive. Part 3 (box at right, 100 ft): Central Av between Carlton Av and Columbus Av, Lakewood Rd (modern Glen Avenue); Central west of Lakewood Rd is modern Lakewood Road.

sheet-23-2.description: The upper part of sheet 23 is drawn at 200 feet to an inch, half the scale of the rest of the sheet, and shows the north-western edge of Lakewood around the Country Club's Golf Links and Newman School. A road curves around the west and north of the golf links and runs east to Hope Chapel Rd., which crosses the right side of the part from top to bottom; 14th St. runs east from Hope Chapel Road, and at the bottom a road lettered Road runs west from it while Lake Drive runs east and curves north-east. The golf links fill most of the part and are almost empty, with a club room and a few small buildings near the western road. The Newman School grounds lie in the lower left, with Lock Hall, a fire-proof building with tile walls and concrete floors, a gymnasium, help quarters and a laundry, heated by steam and lit by electricity. On Hope Chapel Road stand the Hope Presbyterian Church and the Presbyterian Parish House, and west of the road the Seton Inn stands in a large lot. A handful of frame dwellings and garages line Hope Chapel Road and 14th Street. A 4 inch water pipe runs diagonally across the golf links. A north arrow is drawn in the upper right of the links.
notes: Hope Chapel Rd. is North Hope Chapel Road in OpenStreetMap; the road at the top running west from it is Country Club Drive.
Lake Drive meets Hope Chapel Road today about 75 m further south than drawn (North Lake Drive); that junction was left out.

sheet-23-3.description: This part of sheet 23, drawn at 100 feet to an inch in a box at the right of the sheet, shows Central Avenue on the west side of Lakewood between Carlton Avenue and Columbus Avenue. Central Avenue runs across the lower part of the box; Carlton Av. meets it from the south, Lakewood Rd. crosses it from the north, and Columbus Av. runs along the right edge. A short street lettered not named branches off at the lower left. Block 308, a large tract north of Central Avenue, holds a dwelling and a garage set back from the road, and blocks 309 and 316 east of Lakewood Road are laid out in lots with a few frame dwellings and automobile garages; blocks 314 and 315 south of Central Avenue are shown only along their frontage, marked no exposure. A north arrow stands in block 308. Heavy lines frame the box against the golf links drawing above and the Montray Circle part below.
notes: Central Av. west of Lakewood Rd. is now Lakewood Road; the 1928 Lakewood Rd. north of Central Avenue is Glen Avenue; Carlton Av. is Carlton Avenue South.

sheet-24-1.description: The main part of sheet 24, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the residential district on the neck of land between Lake Carasaljo to the north and Lake Manetta to the south, west of the Lakewood business centre. South Lake Drive follows the shore of Lake Carasaljo along the top of the part. Central Avenue crosses the middle from west to east, and the north-south streets crossing it are, from the left, Caranetta Drive, Harrison Pl., Sunset Rd., Kimball Rd., Davis Rd., Bradshaw Rd. and Freeman Rd. at the right edge; Lapsley Lane, also lettered Pine Needle Pl., runs north from Central Avenue at the upper left. South of Central Avenue Caranetta Drive curves east through the blocks above the shore of Lake Manetta, which fills the lower left of the part. The blocks, lettered A to S, are cut into long narrow lots; frame dwellings with automobile garages stand along Central Avenue and the north-south roads, while the blocks near South Lake Drive and the lake shores are still largely vacant. Some lot lines are marked from plans. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches run in the main streets. A compass rose stands at the upper left. Heavy lines divide this part from the strip of Central Avenue west of Caranetta Drive below Lake Manetta and from the blocks south of Lake Caranetta at the lower right.
notes: South Lake Drive junctions lie 7 to 10 m from a fit to the other streets (the modern road along the shore has moved) and were left out.
Caranetta Drive east of Kimball Road lies 11 to 15 m from its 1928 line; those junctions were excluded.
Lapsley Lane is also lettered Pine Needle Pl.

An 8 inch water pipe runs in Central Avenue and a 6 inch pipe in Myrtle Place. A north arrow is drawn in block G and the scale bar at the bottom.

sheet-24-3.description: This part of sheet 24, at the lower right below Lake Caranetta, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the blocks east of Freeman Rd. at the eastern end of the neck between the lakes. South Lake Drive runs east along the south shore of Lake Caranetta and bends south-east along Lake Carasaljo, Central Av. crosses the middle of the part, and Caranetta Drive curves through the lower half, with the end of Lake Manetta at the lower right. Blocks A, B, C and D are cut into narrow lots with frame dwellings, automobile garages and a few brick and tile houses; one building is marked used for auto house, on a concrete block foundation. A heavy double line marks the edge of the part along the lake shore, and a heavy line separates it from the strip of Central Avenue to the west.

sheet-25-1.description: The main part of sheet 25 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the district along the South Branch of the Metedeconk River in the west of Lakewood. At the upper left stand the Jersey Central Power and Light Company works, with boiler, pump and power houses, a 500,000 gallon settling basin and coal piles, and the Seaboard Ice Company beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right. Madison Avenue and River Avenue run down the left side, with Meadow Avenue at the top and Lake Carasaljo and Lake Manetta at the left edge, together with the ends of Central Avenue and South Lake Drive. The river crosses the upper part, and Cedar Bridge Avenue runs diagonally down to the right. Most of the middle of the sheet is vacant land cut into long narrow lots by streets that were laid out but not opened: Waters Avenue and Afton Place are marked not opened, as are Alder and an unnamed street. Fulton Avenue runs down the right side to John, where the Fulton Street Public School stands, with Macedonia Baptist Church on John Street, and houses stand along Cedar Bridge Avenue and Fulton Avenue. Park Avenue is the street at the right. The lower left corner of the sheet is a separate boxed part. A compass rose is at the upper right.
notes: Fulton Avenue is today Martin Luther King Drive and the Park Avenue of the sheet is Ashley Avenue; Madison Avenue and River Avenue are one street changing its name.
The drawn Central Railroad of New Jersey line lies about 8.5 m from the modern Southern Secondary line.
Waters Avenue and Afton Place were never opened.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the west of Lakewood along River Avenue, which runs down the left of the sheet from John Street at the top to the foot of the sheet. John Street crosses the top edge. At the left, between River Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, the blocks 306 and 307 are cut by Manetta Place and Edgewood Court, with Lake View Place east of River Avenue below John Street. Frame dwellings stand on narrow lots along River Avenue and these cross streets. Further down, James Street, Birch and Henry cross River Avenue, with Hotel Lawrence on River Avenue, and a fire department hose company building stands where Pine meets River Avenue; Pine runs south-east across the sheet and Cedar crosses it between Pine and Henry. The large block 208 at the upper right is Pine Woods, an unbuilt tract, and the whole right side of the sheet is blank as far as Fulton Avenue on the right edge. A compass rose stands near the upper right and the scale bar is at the foot. The corner of the sheet at the top right is the junction of John Street and Fulton Avenue.
notes: Fulton Avenue is today Martin Luther King Drive.
Cedar Street and Pine Street were left out of the fit: Pine Street's modern line lies several metres off the drawn one and Lakeview Place was rejected at 8.6 m.
The control points are mostly along River Avenue, so leave-one-out error is large and only the single junction at John Street and Fulton Avenue fixes the rotation.

sheet-27-1.description: The left part of sheet 27 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and is bounded on the right by a heavy line that runs down the middle of the sheet. It shows River Avenue running down the left side from the upper edge, past Prospect, where the Paul Kimball Hospital stands with a contagious ward, to Spruce and the Cedar Ct. Drive loop near the bottom. Prospect runs to the west of River Avenue, with the hospital grounds on its south side. Spruce is drawn with a water pipe and the note not opened, and Cedar Ct. Drive ends in a turning circle. Most of the ground between River Avenue and the heavy line is block 212, which is almost empty except for scattered dwellings and a few outbuildings; blocks 207, 290, 291 and 292 are on the west side of River Avenue and block 295 near the foot. The west edge of the sheet is marked No Exposure. The heavy black line at the right is the railroad, drawn as a double line, and the compass rose stands on it near the middle of the sheet.
notes: The heavy line down the middle is the dividing line between this part and part 2, which shows a different section of River Avenue further south; the two are 800 m apart on the ground.

The modern name of Cedar Ct. Drive is Cedar Court.

sheet-27-2.description: The right part of sheet 27 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows River Avenue running down the right of the heavy dividing line, from High near the top to Cushman at the foot. West of River Avenue is a narrow strip of blocks 292, 293 and 294, with the railroad running alongside; east of it are blocks 295, 296, 297, 347, 348, 350 and 353. At the top High crosses River Avenue with small frame dwellings and a contractor's yard on its north side, and Stirling Pl. joins River Avenue from the west below it with a dotted pipe line. Oak, Pinewood Blvd. and Cushman cross River Avenue at greater distances; the blocks east of River Avenue are drawn with streets marked not named, Wadsworth not opened, and the rest vacant. Houses stand along River Avenue, numbered in the 900s down the right side. Pinewood Blvd. is drawn with six-inch water pipe and a row of small lots with a few frame dwellings and a pump house. The right edge of the sheet is marked No Exposure.
notes: Pinewood Blvd. is today Pine Boulevard.
